title: Study Execution Studio
subtitle: Choose one question. Diagnose one cause. Prove the repair.

missions.title: Restart with one bounded question
missions.brief: Use a small completed output to regain direction.
missions.bring: One accessible question and its scheme, paper, pen and a realistic study window.
missions.output: One independent attempt, strict mark and a named next action.
steps: Choose one question narrow enough for the window; write the reference and subject.
Attempt closed book. Record where you stopped instead of filling gaps from memory of the solution.
Mark each part using the actual scheme; keep unanswered parts visible.
Choose the earliest reasoning break and repair just that prerequisite.
Hide the solution and reattempt the relevant part; label this as a reattempt.
Log the original marked result in the ledger and schedule fresh transfer in the repair workflow.
checks: An original answer exists before opening the scheme.
Earned marks come from the scheme rather than confidence.
The next action names a question or concept, not “study harder”.
traps: A short window need not contain the entire learning cycle.
Planning and timer minutes are not marked output.
missions.transfer: Use a new question after the narrow repair.
missions.prompt: After my independent attempt, use the supplied scheme to identify the first lost marking point and one small repair. Do not award unsupported credit. QUESTION: [...] ANSWER: [...] SCHEME: [...]

missions.title: Biology: build a marking-point paragraph
missions.brief: Turn a broad essay weakness into one accurate, retrievable paragraph.
missions.bring: An actual essay subpart, official/course source and a reliable marking scheme where available.
missions.output: Original paragraph, point-by-point marking and a fresh paragraph written from memory.
steps: Identify the command word and exact scope; list only the subpart you will answer.
Write one paragraph unaided using precise terms and explicit relationships.
Map each sentence to an accepted point; distinguish absent, inaccurate and irrelevant material.
Repair one relationship or missing term using the course source.
Close all references and write the paragraph again without copying sentence order.
Attempt a differently worded subpart and record marks in the appropriate subject workspace.
checks: Correct facts answer the actual command word.
Terminology and relationships survive closed-book recall.
Extra content is not counted as extra marks without scheme support.
traps: Memorising a model answer can conceal inability to adapt.
Do not let an AI invent a national marking point.
missions.transfer: Change “describe” to a source-supported comparison or explanation.
missions.prompt: Check my attempted Biology paragraph against only the supplied source/scheme. Label missing, incorrect and irrelevant points separately. Explain one key correction; do not write a replacement essay until I reattempt. QUESTION: [...] ANSWER: [...] SOURCE: [...]

missions.title: Chemistry: diagnose a calculation chain
missions.brief: Locate the first invalid chemical or mathematical step.
missions.bring: A calculation question, complete working, data and marking source.
missions.output: A trace from chemical model to equation, substitution, units and answer.
steps: Write species, conditions and the target quantity before calculation.
Show the relevant equation or relationship and justify its use.
Carry units through substitution; keep unrounded values until the final step.
Mark the chain and locate the first wrong assumption, stoichiometric relation or arithmetic step.
Repair that step using the source, then recalculate independently.
Use a fresh numerical or condition change and check whether the relationship still applies.
checks: The equation applies under the stated conditions.
Chemical ratios precede arithmetic.
Units, significant figures and final interpretation are checked.
traps: Correct arithmetic cannot rescue an invalid chemical model.
Changing only numbers may provide a weak transfer check.
missions.transfer: Change the required unknown or a stated condition, then choose the method again.
missions.prompt: Review my attempted calculation. Find the earliest invalid assumption or step. Check species, conditions, equation, stoichiometry, units and arithmetic against the supplied source. Give one targeted hint before a full worked answer. QUESTION: [...] WORKING: [...] SOURCE: [...]

missions.title: Physics: choose the model before the formula
missions.brief: Make assumptions, diagrams and limiting cases visible.
missions.bring: A real question, your full attempt and an accepted solution or course reference.
missions.output: A diagram, stated assumptions, justified equation and independently checked result.
steps: Draw a labelled diagram and define positive directions and the system.
State assumptions and identify which principle connects knowns to the unknown.
Derive or rearrange symbolically before inserting values.
Check dimensions, signs and a simple limiting case where applicable.
Compare with the scheme and repair the earliest model-selection error.
Attempt a new geometry, direction or boundary condition and explain the method choice.
checks: Diagram, signs and equations describe the same physical system.
Assumptions are stated rather than silently imported.
A numerical answer includes units and a physical interpretation.
traps: A familiar formula can be inappropriate for the actual constraints.
A dimensional match is necessary in many contexts but does not prove correctness.
missions.transfer: Change the geometry or boundary condition so formula recognition alone is insufficient.
missions.prompt: Inspect my Physics attempt. Before discussing arithmetic, check the diagram, system boundary, assumptions, directions and governing principle. Identify the first inconsistent step and ask one diagnostic question. QUESTION: [...] ATTEMPT: [...] SOURCE: [...]

missions.title: MCQ: separate knowledge from a lucky guess
missions.brief: Use distractors to identify the misconception behind a response.
missions.bring: A short MCQ set, your choices and confidence recorded before checking the key.
missions.output: A marked set with justified distractor rejection and uncertainty labels.
steps: Attempt without the key; mark confidence and any guessed choice immediately.
Check against a trusted key and flag any disputed answer for source review.
For one error, state why your chosen distractor looked attractive.
Explain why the correct choice fits and why each alternative fails under the question conditions.
Test the same principle with a fresh item rather than repeating the answer letter.
Record guesses separately; full marks with unsupported guesses still require follow-up.
checks: Confidence is recorded before the answer key.
Key disputes remain unresolved until checked.
At least one misconception is stated in your own words.
traps: Remembering an answer letter is not retrieval of the principle.
Do not repair an item against a doubtful commercial key.
missions.transfer: Change the context or the attractive distractor, not just the option order.
missions.prompt: I have completed these MCQs. Using the supplied trusted key/source, help me explain the misconception behind my chosen distractor. If the key is unsupported or inconsistent, flag a dispute and stop awarding certainty. ITEM: [...] CHOICE/CONFIDENCE: [...] SOURCE: [...]

missions.title: Practical: interpret supplied data honestly
missions.brief: Distinguish data reasoning from hands-on practical performance.
missions.bring: An authorised supplied-data activity, graph paper/tool and its rubric.
missions.output: A graph or calculation with justified axes, units and a source-labelled conclusion.
steps: Identify independent, dependent and controlled variables from the actual activity.
Choose axes, units, sensible scale and an appropriate representation.
Plot supplied observations without fabricating missing measurements.
Calculate the requested gradient or quantity using a clearly shown method.
Interpret the relationship within the supported range and state uncertainty or limitations.
Mark the reasoning; record hands-on performance only if actually observed under appropriate supervision.
checks: Axes, labels and units are present.
Conclusion follows supplied data, with no invented measurement.
Data interpretation is labelled separately from observed practical performance.
traps: A successful simulation is not proof of competent laboratory technique.
Do not extrapolate beyond the supported range without labelling the assumption.
missions.transfer: Use a new dataset with a changed scale, a missing point or a justified anomalous observation.
missions.prompt: Review my supplied-data interpretation against the activity and rubric. Check variables, axes, units, scale, gradient method and conclusion. Do not invent observations or label this as observed hands-on competence. ACTIVITY: [...] DATA: [...] ATTEMPT: [...]

missions.title: Repair one recurring error
missions.brief: Link a narrow correction to the exact original error.
missions.bring: One original marked attempt with its reference and error ID, and a reliable correction source.
missions.output: A cause, repair, closed-book reattempt and separate fresh-transfer result.
steps: Choose a recurring error using lost marks and frequency, not discomfort alone.
Name the cause: missing knowledge, wrong model, retrieval failure, misreading or execution slip.
Use one small source section to repair the cause.
Close the source and reattempt the original step; keep assisted and independent work distinct.
Solve a fresh question that changes an important feature and mark it.
Use the existing repair workflow to attach the result to the original attempt; retain failed checks.
checks: The correction targets a cause rather than merely restating the right answer.
Fresh evidence links to the exact original error.
A failed check keeps the repair open.
traps: Repeatedly copying a solution can create misleading familiarity.
A general diary note cannot close an unrelated error chain.
missions.transfer: Choose a structurally different question testing the repaired principle.
missions.prompt: Diagnose this original marked error. Separate symptom from cause. Propose one bounded source-based repair and one structurally different transfer task. Do not mark the error closed until independent evidence is supplied. ORIGINAL: [...] SOURCE: [...]

missions.title: Retest without leaking the answer
missions.brief: Check retention using fresh material after the actual scheduled delay.
missions.bring: A due error chain, unseen question and trusted marking source.
missions.output: A dated independent retest linked to the original error.
steps: Open the due queue and choose the exact original error being checked.
Choose unseen material; hide old solutions, notes and hints.
Attempt independently and record assistance if it occurs.
Mark strictly and retain the first result even if it fails.
If successful, submit it through the linked retest flow; if not, reopen the narrow repair.
Choose the next check based on actual performance, not calendar completion alone.
checks: Retest date is actual, not future or backfilled.
No hidden answer exposure is represented as independent.
Result links to the correct original attempt.
traps: An overdue item is unfinished work, not personal failure.
A scheduled reminder is not evidence that a check occurred.
missions.transfer: Use a changed context that still requires the repaired principle.
missions.prompt: Help me prepare a retest without revealing the answer. Use the original error only to identify the principle; propose an unseen task for source checking. Wait for my independent attempt before feedback. ERROR: [...] ALLOWED SOURCE: [...]

missions.title: Review a timed paper for the next useful repair
missions.brief: Convert a paper score into a small, actionable diagnosis.
missions.bring: An actual timed paper, completed answers, marking scheme and timing notes.
missions.output: Strict total, loss classification and three ranked follow-up actions.
steps: Complete the paper under the intended conditions and record interruptions.
Mark by question and accepted point; retain zeros and skipped parts.
Classify avoidable losses separately from concepts you could not retrieve.
Find repeated causes across questions; distinguish knowledge, timing and execution.
Select at most three repairs and put one fresh check first.
Keep score trends tied to comparable papers and conditions; preserve raw marks and totals.
checks: Percentage has the actual earned and total marks.
Interrupted or assisted papers are labelled.
Next actions specify a topic, source and fresh question.
traps: Different paper difficulty limits direct score comparisons.
A high total can conceal repeated weaknesses in a small topic.
missions.transfer: Use a second paper and inspect whether the same cause reappears.
missions.prompt: Analyse my already marked paper. Preserve earned/total marks and testing conditions. Group lost marks by demonstrated cause, identify recurring errors, and select at most three concrete repairs. Do not invent rankings, predicted grades or mastery. MARKED SUMMARY: [...]

missions.title: Weekly review with realistic capacity
missions.brief: Use completed work and available time to choose a manageable next week.
missions.bring: The last seven days of actual attempts, open repairs and known commitments.
missions.output: A short evidence review and a capacity-aware plan with catch-up space.
steps: Count completed marked work separately from lectures, plans and timer minutes.
Review the three most repeated errors and due unfinished checks.
Estimate usable windows after sleep, meals, classes and other commitments.
Choose a small set of question or repair outcomes that fit those windows.
Reserve catch-up space; defer low-priority collection and administrative work.
At the next review compare actual outputs with the plan and adjust one assumption.
checks: Plans fit real available windows.
Protected rest is not silently reallocated.
Review includes failed and unfinished work without hiding it.
traps: More scheduled hours do not establish better learning.
A backlog needs prioritisation, not an ever-longer daily list.
missions.transfer: Replan after losing one study window without borrowing from sleep.
missions.prompt: Using only these completed outputs, open errors and available windows, propose a realistic next week. Protect stated sleep and commitments, reserve catch-up capacity, and defer work that cannot fit. Do not treat plans as achievements. EVIDENCE: [...] WINDOWS: [...]
